back_translation: "Be silent before Me, O islands; let the peoples receive new strength. Let them approach, then let them speak; let us draw near together for judgment.

Who has aroused one from the east and called him in righteousness to His service? He hands nations over before him and subdues kings before him. He makes them like dust with his sword, like driven stubble with his bow.
He pursues them and passes on safely, along a path his feet have never trodden before.
Who has done this and accomplished it? Who has called the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD — the First, and with those who are last — I am He."
The islands have seen and are afraid; the ends of the earth tremble. They draw near and come forward.
Each one helps his neighbor and says to his brother, "Be strong!"
The craftsman encourages the goldsmith; he who strikes with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil. He says of the weld, "It is good," then nails the idol down so it will not wobble.
"But you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham My friend —
you whom I brought from the ends of the earth and called from its farthest corners, I said to you, 'You are My servant.' I have chosen you and have not cast you off.
Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; surely I will help you; surely I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.
Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will become as nothing and will perish.
You will look for them but will not find them. Those who wage war against you will come to nothing at all.
For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand and say to you: Do not fear; I will help you.
Do not fear, O worm Jacob, O little people of Israel. I will help you," declares the LORD. "Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Behold, I will make you into a new, sharp threshing sledge with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and make the hills like chaff.
You will winnow them and the wind will carry them away; a whirlwind will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD and glory in the Holy One of Israel.
"The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the bare heights and springs in the midst of the valleys. I will turn the wilderness into a pool of water and the parched land into flowing springs.
I will plant cedars, acacias, myrtles, and olive trees in the wilderness. I will set cypresses, planes, and pines together in the desert,
so that all may see and know, may consider and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it."
"Present your case," says the LORD. "Bring your proofs," says the King of Jacob.
"Let them bring them and tell us what will happen. Declare the former things — what they were — so that we may consider them and know their outcome. Or announce to us the things to come.
Declare what will happen afterward, so that we may know that you are gods. Indeed, do something — good or evil — so that we may be amazed and behold it together.
Behold, you are nothing at all, and your work is utterly empty. Whoever chooses you is detestable.
"I have aroused one from the north, and he has come — one from the rising of the sun who calls on My name. He will trample rulers as one tramples mortar, as a potter treads the clay.
Who declared this from the beginning so that we might know, or beforehand so that we might say, 'He was right'? No one declared it, no one announced it, no one heard any words from you.
I was the first to say to Zion, 'Behold, here they are!' And I have given to Jerusalem a herald of good news.
I look, but there is no one; among them there is not a single counselor. When I ask them, there is not a word of answer.
Behold, they are all a delusion; their works are worthless; their cast images are mere wind and emptiness.
